fields.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.
fields.note: The requirement summary tracks the Foreclosure section closely: 90-day notice to quit, lease running past 90 days, English/Spanish notice within 10 business days, door posting plus certified and regular mail, common-area posting for more than 10 units, creditor notice under the court rules, NOTICE TO TENANTS with monetary offers, written acceptance with five-day review, and the pressure-tactic list.

fields.quoted_span: the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence
fields.note: The 10-business-day English/Spanish notice and the five-day review period are also in the document.
The rule's effective date is empty, and the guide states no effective date for the Foreclosure Fairness Act provisions.

fields.quoted_span: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale
fields.note: The guide presents these as current requirements, with no mention of repeal or a sunset, so in_force is consistent with it.

fields.quoted_span:
Month-
to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirements.
fields.note: min_units=1 is backed by 'one or more residential rental units'. The creditor and acquirer duties are described in the document. The document says nothing contradicting the other coverage fields, which are empty.

The document cites 2A:50-70(c)2 for common-area posting, 2A:50-69 et seq. for the notices and the Foreclosure Fairness Act, and 2A:50-71(b) for pressure tactics. The aliases are supported. The 90-day notice rests on case law, as the review note says.
